newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Buba's Schmidhuber sees EMU going ahead on time.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Schmidhuber sees EMU going ahead on time.

text.p: Bundesbank board member Peter Schmidhuber said on Friday he thought European Economic and monetary union (EMU) would go ahead on time in January 1999.
"I don't think that the starting point of European Monetary Union will be delayed," Schmidhuber told Reuters.
He was in Dublin to give a private briefing to members of the Irish Institute of European Affairs.
He said that the German government had the power to keep Germany's budget deficit in the range of three percent, thereby allowing Germany to meet the Maastricht criteria for entry to EMU.

"It depends on the political will of the government and, on the other hand, on the development of macro-economic factors. The nominal growth rate of GNP is a very important factor in this respect," Schmidhuber said.
He said there could be no window dressing or one-off measures to qualify for EMU and said factors such as sustainability were very important.
"Countries must have a solid budgetary policy not only for one year, 1997, but for years to come," he said.
Schmidhuber said the public debate on EMU had been shortened to just two numbers, the budget deficit target of three percent and a public debt/GDP target of 60 percent.
But deciding who would qualify for EMU was a very complicated procedure in which lots of macro-economic elements and features of financial policy had to be considered, he said.
Schmidhuber said that the independence of the European Central Bank was also very important, "an overriding element of the whole system".

Asked about the setting up of a so-called "Stability Council", Schmidhuber said this would have to be clarified. He said there would be great reservations in Germany, and not just at the Bundesbank, if the Stability Council was a countervailing power to the European Central Bank.
